signature.name: Zagreb Cathedral
signature.detail: Croatia's tallest church and the city's defining spire, with a richly restored interior and a treasury. Go early morning to have the square in front mostly to yourself, and dress modestly since it is an active place of worship.

signature.name: St. Mark's Church
signature.detail: Famous for its brightly tiled roof bearing the city and national coats of arms, sitting on the cobbled heart of Gornji Grad. It is a short walk up from Ban Jelačić Square; check opening hours before going as interior access is limited.

signature.name: Gornji Grad
signature.detail: The old upper town of lanes, squares and historic buildings that gives Zagreb its character. Wander it on foot in the late afternoon, combining it with St. Mark's Church and the Stone Gate nearby.

signature.name: Ban Jelačić Square
signature.detail: The central square and meeting point of the city, ringed by cafés and the starting point for most walks. Come in the evening when it is liveliest, and use it as your orientation point for the lower town.

signature.name: Dolac Market
signature.detail: The colourful open-air market where locals buy produce, cheese and flowers. Arrive before noon for the fullest stalls, and bring small cash for the vendors.

signature.name: Stone Gate
signature.detail: A medieval gate that survived a fire and now shelters a shrine with a revered icon, still visited by pilgrims. It sits on the walk between the square and Gornji Grad, so it is easy to include on a walking route.

signature.name: Lotrščak Tower
signature.detail: A historic tower with a daily cannon firing at noon and views over the old town. Climb it around midday to catch the cannon, and note the small entry fee.

signature.name: Museum of Broken Relationships
signature.detail: A quirky, moving museum of objects donated after breakups, one of the city's most talked-about sights. It is compact, so allow about an hour; buy tickets on arrival.

signature.name: Mirogoj Cemetery
signature.detail: A grand park-like cemetery with arcades and domes, often described as an open-air gallery. It is a short bus or tram ride from the centre; go in daylight and dress for the weather.
